item.title: Midwest is overwhelmed by rainfall caused by rising temps (which will only get worse)
item.description: Severe storms in the Midwest have cause widespread flooding. Climate experts say extreme rainfall has already gotten worse in the region and will keep intensifying.
item.content:encoded: Severe storms in the Midwest have cause widespread flooding. Climate experts say extreme rainfall has already gotten worse in the region and will keep intensifying.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Sommer

item.title: Testimony begins in the trial of rapper Tupac Shakur's 1996 killing
item.description: Opening statements began Monday in the murder trial of rapper Tupac Shakur. The man implicated in the 1996 killing in Las Vegas is a former gang member.
item.content:encoded: Opening statements began Monday in the murder trial of rapper Tupac Shakur. The man implicated in the 1996 killing in Las Vegas is a former gang member.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere and how Hollywood fails to protect women
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Marlow Stern, chief correspondent for Variety, about actress Hayden Panettiere's life and career after her death at age 36.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Marlow Stern, chief correspondent for Variety, about actress Hayden Panettiere's life and career after her death at age 36.

item.title: A uranium revival brings new worries to tribal lands
item.description: Uranium production has been revived in the US Southwest. Tribal communities there who suffered illnesses from previous development are worried nuclear energy will harm them again.
item.content:encoded: Uranium production has been revived in the US Southwest. Tribal communities there who suffered illnesses from previous development are worried nuclear energy will harm them again.

item.title: One Florida county sees the ripple effects of its cooperation with ICE
item.description: Walton County, Fla., relies heavily on immigrant labor for its booming construction and tourism industries. We look at how county sheriffs' cooperation with ICE affects things.

item.title: A summer camp celebrating Kazakh culture helps adopted kids connect with their culture
item.description: Families of children adopted from Kazakhstan meet every summer in New Hampshire's lake country to celebrate the food and culture of their country of origin.
item.content:encoded: Families of children adopted from Kazakhstan meet every summer in New Hampshire's lake country to celebrate the food and culture of their country of origin.

item.title: Palestinian family in West Bank fear settler violence will rob them of home
item.description: The family of a Palestinian-American man remain holed up in his West Bank home for more than a week, after Israeli settlers laid siege to the house and the Israeli army then turned it into a closed military area.

item.title: Florida GOP race draws accusations of carpetbagging
item.description: "Carpetbagger" describes people who move somewhere to run for office. In Southwest Florida, six former congressional hopefuls from other states are taking their shot in this conservative stronghold.

item.title: Cities are adopting new data center standards as public opposition grows
item.description: As the number of data centers across the U.S. continues to increase, so does public opposition. That has some cities changing their standards for what acceptable data center development looks like.

item.title: A professor's death brings new focus to how Black academics are treated
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Professor Shaun Harper about the intense media scrutiny of British sociologist Jason Arday and how the scholar's death has reverberated in Black academic circles.
